Oyster Therapeutics · brandmark brainstorm, round twelve

Two proteins, one pearl

Proteins first, the oyster only in the silhouette. Round eleven had drifted back to a shell: a circle, with lines that read as growth rings. Here the circle and the shell lines are gone. BRD4 and VHL keep close to their real traced proportions and are drawn as molecular surfaces, the scalloped edge of a space-filling model. Each is placed to hold half of the pearl, and the two are docked along their whole facing side at a hairline gap, so the mouth is closed. Together they happen to make the rounded, lumpy shape of an oyster. The pearl is split along the seam and held by its linker. Structures: PDB 5T35, Gadd et al., Nat. Chem. Biol. 2017; the degrader is drawn generically.

BRD4 and VHL as molecular surfaces, close to their real proportions, each holding half of the pearl and docked along their whole facing side. No shell lines: the oyster is only in the shape the two make together.

Proteins first: you see two molecules meeting round a pearl, and then an oyster.
